result.note: Tests the summit venue, the Finland and Denmark partnership outcomes, and the EFTA TEPA, Norway and Varanasi details.

questions.prompt: In May 2026, the 3rd India-Nordic Summit was held in which city?
questions.explain: The 3rd India-Nordic Summit concluded in Oslo on 18 May 2026. Prime Minister Modi held bilateral meetings there with the leaders of Finland, Denmark, Iceland and Norway. Stockholm hosted the 2018 edition and Copenhagen the 2022 edition.
questions.source: The summit follows previous editions in Stockholm (2018) and Copenhagen (2022).

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's bilateral outcomes at the India-Nordic Summit in May 2026:
items: India and Finland elevated ties to a Strategic Partnership in Digitalization and Sustainability.
The India-Denmark Green Strategic Partnership was launched in 2022.
India and Finland will jointly host the World Circular Economic Forum in Gandhinagar in September 2026.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the India-Denmark Green Strategic Partnership was launched in 2020. India and Finland also committed to double bilateral trade by 2030.
questions.source: Modi and Acting Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen reviewed progress under the India-Denmark Green Strategic Partnership, launched in 2020.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's engagement with Nordic countries as reported in May 2026:
items: The India-European Free Trade Association (EFTA) Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement entered into force in October 2025.
The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research's collaboration on floating offshore wind technology is with SINTEF, Norway's largest independent research organisation.
India and Denmark have a joint Smart Laboratory on Clean Rivers in Varanasi.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: All three statements are correct. The SINTEF floating offshore wind collaboration was the centrepiece of five CSIR agreements with Norwegian research bodies. Norway and Iceland fall under the EFTA TEPA, while Sweden, Denmark and Finland fall under the India-EU FTA.
questions.source: The centrepiece is a collaboration on floating offshore wind technology with SINTEF, Norway's largest independent research organisation.
